5.1.1.3 Lateral flow analysis 
Lateral flow assays (LFAs) are hand -held devices based on immunochromatography on 
paper strips such as nitrocellulose. The sample is applied to one end of the strip and migrates 
by capillary action to the opposite end of the strip. While migrating along the strip the sample 
molecules first bind to an immobilized detection antibody conjugated to gold nanoparticles 
or dyes. The antibody -antigen complex further continues to migrate along the strip and is 
captured in the detection zone by a capture antibody, resulting in a visible change of colour. 
Several LFAs for detection of ricin and RCA120 have been developed, 34,44,46 and a number 
of them are commercially available, e.g. 
 KDTB Gold Assay, NBC-sys (Saint Chamond, France) 
 miPROTECT, miprolab (Göttingen, Germany) 
 BioThreat Alert,Tetracore (Rockville, USA) 
Usually, LFAs are less sensitive than classical sandwich-ELISA with detection limits in the 
low ng/ml-range. I
title: Recommended Operating Procedures for Analysis in the Verification of Chemical Disarmament

text:
miPROTECT, miprolab (Göttingen, Germany) 
 BioThreat Alert,Tetracore (Rockville, USA) 
Usually, LFAs are less sensitive than classical sandwich-ELISA with detection limits in the 
low ng/ml-range. Instead, they are much faster to perform delivering results are within 10–
20 min, an d can be handled by first responders and field investigation teams. Note that 
current LFAs detect ricin as well as RCA120. 
Currently publications on comparative LFA validation studies are sparse in the open 
literature.58,59 Some of the mentioned commercial LFA have successfully been applied in a 
recent ricin proficiency test, but more work has to be undertaken to evaluate these field tests 
comprehensively.33,34,37 It is of utmost importance to test the performance of LFAs on a range 
of different spiked and unspiked complex matrices, since the multitude of relevant 
substances present in complex environmental matrices poses a serious challenge for reliable 
detection. Therefore, detailed knowledge of the specific scope of applications and the 
limitations of different products is necessary to evaluate the results obtained purposefully. 
Performance characteristics: 
 Time to result: 10–20 min

5.1.1.4 Antibody response 
Anti-ricin immunoglobulin G (IgG), IgG1, IgG2a and IgA antibodies have been reported in 
mouse sera after ricin exposure. Production of IgA antibodies against ricin A-chain and B-
chain after ricin immunization can protect epithelial cells from ricin into xication. 60 
Determination of anti-ricin IgG in mouse sera stimulated with a ricin vaccine candidate has 
been reported under a project of the US Army Medical Research Institute of Infectious 
Diseases.61 Comparing with direct de termination of ricin toxin in the biomedical samples, 
the determination of ricin stimulated antibody is rare.

5.3 Activity assays 
In the case of malevolent use or release of ricin, the discrimination of functionally active and 
denatured ricin is important to determine the threat level of a sample and to take appropriate 
actions with respect to emergency operating schedules, forensic analysis and therapy. 
Information on ricin’s activity can only be obtained from functional assays that, depending 
on the assay format, detect the A-chain activity (depurination activity), the B-chain activity 
(carbohydrate binding), or both. In vitro assays, like adenine -release assays or cell -free 
translation assays based on rabbit reticulocyte lysate, analyse the depurination activity of the 
ricin A chain .70–76 The glycan binding function of the ricin B -subunit can be detected by 
enzyme-linked lectin assays (ELLA) where the toxin is enriched on carbohydrates and 
detected via specific antibodies .49 However, the detection of the activity of the isolated 
subchains provides no information o
title: Recommended Operating Procedures for Analysis in the Verification of Chemical Disarmament

text:
lectin assays (ELLA) where the toxin is enriched on carbohydrates and 
detected via specific antibodies .49 However, the detection of the activity of the isolated 
subchains provides no information on the activity of the intact 64 kDa ricin molecule. 
Therefore, the detection of active ricin optimally requires assays detecting both subchains. 
Promising approaches, based on immunocapture assays combined with spectrometric 
measurement of adenine release have been developed and applied in forensic 
investigations.77–79 
The principle of this method is the capture of the ricin by magnetic beads coated with 
antibodies directed against chain B, the elimination of sample interferents, and reaction of 
ricin chain A with its specific RNA substrate that results in the release of adenine, mimicking

5.3.2 Cell-based assays 
Cell-based cytotoxicity assays display the full biological activity of ricin by displaying 
i) the binding of ricin to carbohydrates on the cell surface, 
ii) the subsequent internalization and retrograde transport of ricin including the 
translocation of ricin A into the cytosol and 
iii) the depurinating activity of ricin A on the 28S rRNA leading to an arrest of 
protein synthesis and eventually cell death. 
Currently practised assays depict the cytotoxic effect of ricin on different cell types either as 
end-point assa ys or in real -time.45,48– 83 Usually African green monkey (Vero) cells or 
macrophage cell lines are used to display ricin’s cytotoxic activity. In the classical assay 
format, cells are seeded into cell culture plates and incubated for 4 –48 h with increasing 
concentrations of ricin. In the en d point assay, the number of viable cells is determined by 
addition of coloured tetrazolium dyes (MTT, WST and others) whic
title: Recommended Operating Procedures for Analysis in the Verification of Chemical Disarmament

text:
d incubated for 4 –48 h with increasing 
concentrations of ricin. In the en d point assay, the number of viable cells is determined by 
addition of coloured tetrazolium dyes (MTT, WST and others) which are converted into 
differently coloured soluble or insoluble formazan derivatives by NAD(P)H-dependent 
cellular oxidoreductase enzymes. The reduction of the tetrazolium dyes reflects the cellular 
metabolic activity due to NAD(P)H flux. As readout, the absorbance of the coloured solution 
is measured spectrophotometrically. Alternatively, real-time assays display the cytotoxicity 
by measuring the impedance of a cell layer treated with di fferent concentrations of ricin. 48 
This technique uses an impedance sensor technology to noninvasively and label -free 
quantify cell viability, based on cell number, morphology and adhesion in real -time. The 
cells are seeded in special “E-plates” into which microelectrodes are integrated. Low voltage 
application leads to the generation of an elect ric field, which is differentially modulated by 
the cells. The higher the number of cells attached to the plate surface, the higher is the 
impedance monitored by the sensor system as a read -out
title: Recommended Operating Procedures for Analysis in the Verification of Chemical Disarmament

text:
ct ric field, which is differentially modulated by 
the cells. The higher the number of cells attached to the plate surface, the higher is the 
impedance monitored by the sensor system as a read -out for cell viability. Compared to 
endpoint assays, the most important advantage of the impedance measurement is the online 
monitoring of cellular status, which offers the possibility to better standardize the assay. 
Depending on the exact experimental conditions used, the detection limits for ricin analysis 
in cell-based bioassays have been described as being between 0.01 ng/ml and 0.8 ng/ml even 
from complex matrices after different cell cultivation times (ranging from 4 to 48 h). When 
directly compared in a given experimental setting, the cytotoxic effect produced by highly 
purified ricin is about 300 -times higher than the cytotoxicity induced by highly purified 
RCA120.38 
A certain limitation of the assay form at is its limited matrix tolerance, so effects on cell 
viability produced by unknown sample components have to be thoroughly controlled. To 
exclude cytotoxic effects caused by irrelevant matrix components or to differentiate from 
other ribosome inactivating toxins su
title: Recommended Operating Procedures for Analysis in the Verification of Chemical Disarmament

text:
uced by unknown sample components have to be thoroughly controlled. To 
exclude cytotoxic effects caused by irrelevant matrix components or to differentiate from 
other ribosome inactivating toxins such as abrin or shigatoxins exerting the same cytotoxic 
effect, a functional blockade by anti -ricin antibodies is required to demonstrate specificity. 
On the other hand, a clear advantage of cell -based cytotoxicity assays is to display the full 
biologic activity of ricin. This is especially important since there is information available 
that under certain denaturing conditions the carbohydrate -binding property of the ricin B 
chain is destroyed whereas the enzymatic activity of the A chain is retai ned, even in the 
presence of an intact disulfide bond between the A and B chain.84 
Performance characteristics: 
 Time to result: 4–48 h 
 Detection limit: 0.01–0.8 ng/ml 
 Matrix tolerance: limited

5.4 Forensic investigation 
5.4.1 Detection of ricin originating material 
Seeds of Ricinus communis plant contain several low molecular weight chemicals, which 
can be used to classify material originating from the seeds. 
The best known chemical is ricinine (CAS 524-40-3) – a small alkaloid – which has been 
suggested as an indirect surrogate marker for ricin originating material. 85,86 This chemical 
can be used to classify samples or their extracts rapidly for non-purified material originating 
from ricin. Screening and identification of ricinine would be simple and fast using nuclear 
magnetic resonance spectroscopy (NMR) or mass spectrometry (MS). Ricinine has also been 
used as a clinical marker for ricin exposure.87–89 
In addition to ricinine, several other char acteristic chemicals have been identified in ricin 
seed extracts: e.g. ricinyl-alanine and N-demethylricinine.90 
It has also been suggested that t he small molecules can be used to classify th
title: Recommended Operating Procedures for Analysis in the Verification of Chemical Disarmament

text:
char acteristic chemicals have been identified in ricin 
seed extracts: e.g. ricinyl-alanine and N-demethylricinine.90 
It has also been suggested that t he small molecules can be used to classify the different 
Ricinus communis cultivars.90 
5.4.2 NMR analysis 
Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy can be used to study metabolome of the 
ricin-containing sample.89,90 This can include study of selected target chemicals, e.g. ricinine, 
or more comprehensive analysis of the metabolome. NMR spectra can be used to classify 
ricin samples using principal component analysis (PCA), e.g. for forensic purposes.89 
In the NMR analysis, proton ( 1H) spectra are measured. As NMR will detect all hydrogen -
containing chemicals in the sample, the proteins should be removed from the sample before 
the analysis so that their signals would not dominate the spectrum. A simple way to prepare 
the NMR sample is to use molecular weight cut-off (MWCO) filters, either 3 kDa or 10 kDa, 
to remove the larger molecules from the sample. This will also make the NMR sample safer 
to handle. The sample collected on the MWCO filter can be used form other analysis. 
A clear advantage of the NMR analysis
title: Recommended Operating Procedures for Analysis in the Verification of Chemical Disarmament

text:
e larger molecules from the sample. This will also make the NMR sample safer 
to handle. The sample collected on the MWCO filter can be used form other analysis. 
A clear advantage of the NMR analysis of small molecules is that it is a fast method. 
However, it will provide only indirect indication of the presence of Ricinus communis -
originating material. 
Performance characteristics: 
 Time to result: 15–60 min 
 Detection limit: ca. 0.1–1 µg/ml* 
 Matrix tolerance: limited 
5.4.3 Detection of DNA 
For the R. communis or crude ricin contaminated samples, detection of the presence of DNA 
encoding the gene for ricin can provide the complementary information on the presence of 
ricin, since a positive result is revealed by the presence of R. communis DNA, but not ricin 
itself. In the real time polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) method, most important aspects

inhibitory substances in a rather complex matrix by suitable DNA extraction and purification

As the toxin -specific DNA is generally more stable than the protein toxin itself, qPCR 
method can be applied to the sample of ricin protein denatured or degraded. There are cases 
where DNA is not expected to be found in the samples: e.g. clinical samples of exposure 
patients or when purified ricin has been present. Due to this, negative PCR result does not 
always mean that no ricin is present. 
5.4.5 Molecular weight determination 
One of the characteristic features of ricin is the molecular weight of the intact protein, but it 
can’t be used as such to identify the protein. A rough molecular weight range can be obtained 
from Western Blot, gel or capillary electrophoresis. More accurate d ata can
title: Recommended Operating Procedures for Analysis in the Verification of Chemical Disarmament

text:
the intact protein, but it 
can’t be used as such to identify the protein. A rough molecular weight range can be obtained 
from Western Blot, gel or capillary electrophoresis. More accurate d ata can be measured 
using MALDI –TOF. Most informative data can be obtained from full scan LC –ESI/MS 
spectra.38 It should be noted that the method is clearly less sensitive than LC –ESI/MS/MS 
identification of tryptic peptides. 
The mass spectra will show a complex pattern including isoforms, charge distribution and 
isotopic patterns. Using spectral deconvolution, these spectra can be transformed into spectra 
of singly charged species, the isoforms of the protein. This molecular ions pattern, therefore 
shows the distribution of the isoforms, which for ricin protein means differently glycosylated 
proteins. 
The glycosylation patterns have been shown to differ between different cultivars. 67,92 This 
information could possibly be used for forensic purposes. 
5.4.6 Glycosylation 
Determination of the glycosylation of ricin is an additional feature for identification of ricin, 
which might be helpful in cases where forensic evidence is needed, e.g. for verifying the 
source of ricin toxin
title: Recommended Operating Procedures for Analysis in the Verification of Chemical Disarmament

text:
on of the glycosylation of ricin is an additional feature for identification of ricin, 
which might be helpful in cases where forensic evidence is needed, e.g. for verifying the 
source of ricin toxin. Here, the glycosylation pattern or the glycan structures could be used 
to either compare different sample materials or even estimate the cultivar. 
There are three different ways of detecting the ricin glycosylation. The first method is based 
on analysing the sample with LC–MS followed by deconvolution of the spectra as described 
in paragraph 5.2.4. This method will not give direct information on the glycans themselves, 
but rather a glycosylation pattern. In the second method, the glycopeptides produced in 
enzymatic digestion would be detected and identified using mass spectrometric methods. In 
this method, the difficulty would be the data processing required for detecting the 
glycopeptides in the sample. The third method would be based on enzymatic deglycosylation 
of the sample proteins and analysis of the glycans separately. For this method, the ricin in 
the sample would need to be purified in order to avoid producing a mixture glycans 
originating from different proteins.
title: Recommended Operating Procedures for Analysis in the Verification of Chemical Disarmament

text:
proteins and analysis of the glycans separately. For this method, the ricin in 
the sample would need to be purified in order to avoid producing a mixture glycans 
originating from different proteins. 
Currently, little information is available on the glycosylation of different cultivars and its 
possible changes due to different growth conditions and stages of seed development.

7. Samples 
The sample type s possibly arriving to a laboratory depend stron gly on the scenario. A 
laboratory planning to develop ricin analysis methods should assess possible scenarios 
together with e.g. national authorities or other laboratories. This way they can get 
understanding on what types of samples to expect. 
In different scenarios, the persons taking the samples can be from totally different fields. 
The analysis laboratory should inform the sampling personnel or in the best case train them 
on the best sampling practises and sample types. Also, proper sample packaging and 
handling is essential for protection of the sample as well as personnel involved. It can be 
beneficial to develop a sampling kit and/or easy-to-use instructions, which could cover, e.g. 
sampling, packaging, labelling, storage and transport. 
Some of the sa mple matrices are quite well defined (e.g. urine or milk) and method 
development can be done in advance and, also, vali
title: Recommended Operating Procedures for Analysis in the Verification of Chemical Disarmament

text:
r, e.g. 
sampling, packaging, labelling, storage and transport. 
Some of the sa mple matrices are quite well defined (e.g. urine or milk) and method 
development can be done in advance and, also, validated to a good level. Some matrices, 
however, are quite variable (e.g. soil or food) and it may be difficult to develop a method, 
which covers all possible variations. In the latter case, it is essential to include some type of 
control sample in the sample preparation and analysis process. This could include, but is not 
limited to, spiking controls where the unknown sample is spiked with a known amount of 
ricin to detect matrix interferences. 
7.1 Environmental samples 
The validity of environmental samples for analysis of the presence of ricin depends greatly 
on the case. Detection of ricin in an environmental sample would require that ricin protein 
is stable in the matrix until the sampling. The source of ricin in the s ample can have effect 
on the stability and the sampling procedures. Several different scenarios for environmental 
sampling can be imagined, e.g. waste material from castor oil production, deposition of ricin 
powder from a terrorist use on surfaces or a pool
title: Recommended Operating Procedures for Analysis in the Verification of Chemical Disarmament

text:
cedures. Several different scenarios for environmental 
sampling can be imagined, e.g. waste material from castor oil production, deposition of ricin 
powder from a terrorist use on surfaces or a pool of liquid (after washing or rain). 
One of the challenges of environmental samples is finding suitable sampling locations. For 
chemical warfare agents, such as nerve agents and sulphur mustard, there are hand -held 
continuously measuring detectors, which can be used to locate hot-spot in the sampling area. 
For ricin, no such detectors are available. The best way for on -site detection of ricin are 
lateral flow analysis (LFA) or biosensor approaches, which need to be further analysed in 
the future to highlight their practical application and limitations (see paragraph 5.1.4). 
Required sample preparation can be direct analysis or extraction. Also, different sample 
purification and/or enrichment methods may be needed. 
7.2 Plant material 
Ricinus Communis can be found in different cultivars with different levels of purification. 
The most common cultivars are R. C. Gibsonii (Zimbabwe), R. C. Zanzibariensis (Tanzania 
and Kenya), R. C. Carcimenta (Tanzania), R. C. Impala (Tanzania)
title: Recommended Operating Procedures for Analysis in the Verification of Chemical Disarmament

text:
tivars with different levels of purification. 
The most common cultivars are R. C. Gibsonii (Zimbabwe), R. C. Zanzibariensis (Tanzania 
and Kenya), R. C. Carcimenta (Tanzania), R. C. Impala (Tanzania), R. C. Sanguineus (Spain 
and Tanzania) and R. C. Dehradun (India). Different experiments in LC –MS and NMR 
metabolomics have been developed to characterize these cultivars. 93–96 In order to analyse 
the seeds, a seeds extraction is required by grinding in NaCl at 0.5 M (30 ml for 10 g of 
seeds), pH 4 and shaking overnight. If the plant material is just a raw extract with no 
purification, oil elimination is necessary by manual acetone or hexane extraction and the

identification in the plant material extract, purification and/or enrichment methods may be 
required. After dissolution of the dried residue in acidic water, purification can be achieved 
on 30 kDa MWCO filter or by LC/UV with an ion exchange column followed by LC on gel

7.3 Biomedical samples 
Detection of ricin in biomed ical samples is of importance for medico -legal and forensic 
purposes on demonstrating the proof of ricin intoxication events , and for supporting 
information for medical therapy. All intoxicated biomedical samples such as blood, tissues 
are complicated. For ricin intoxicated biomedical samples (blood, tissue, etc.), sample 
entrapment and enrichment procedures using affinity mod
title: Recommended Operating Procedures for Analysis in the Verification of Chemical Disarmament

text:
intoxicated biomedical samples such as blood, tissues 
are complicated. For ricin intoxicated biomedical samples (blood, tissue, etc.), sample 
entrapment and enrichment procedures using affinity modules are usually employed. Useful 
affinity-based capturing modules include, antibody (in various forms such as poly antibody, 
monoantibody, Fc fusion of an antibody, etc.), galactose (binding to galactose -binding site 
in ricin), and RCA120 (binding to sugar moiety in ricin). Some nanomater ial-based 
conjugates are expected to perform potential advantages in capturing procedures. 
When using affinity module, the cross -reactivity of affinity module for ricin and RCA120 
should be kept in mind and carefully investigated so as to avoid the RCA120 aroused false-
positive problem. 
8. Applications 
Ricin analysis can be related to a wide range of scenarios from normal life situations 
(e.g. testing of ricin seed pulp remaining after castor oil extraction) to emergency situations 
(e.g. large scale use of ricin against civilian population). In order to prepare for all kinds of 
situations, best approach would be to develop a toolbox of methods, which could then be 
applied as seen appro
title: Recommended Operating Procedures for Analysis in the Verification of Chemical Disarmament

text:
ge scale use of ricin against civilian population). In order to prepare for all kinds of 
situations, best approach would be to develop a toolbox of methods, which could then be 
applied as seen appropriate. 
The following applications are using principles and methods discussed in paragraphs 4–6 in 
suitable combination to solve the question at hand. 
8.1 Proficiency tests 
From a diagnostic point of view, ricin detection is challenging for a number of reasons: 
i. Ricin is rapidly metabolized after incorporation, limiting the tim e window for 
successful detection and identification. The clinical symptoms induced by ricin are 
unspecific and a number of naturally occurring diseases caused by pathogens have 
to be taken into account as differential diagnosis. 
ii. Ricin is toxic in the absence of the producing organism R. communis and its genetic 
information, so that nucleic acid -based methods cannot reliably be applied. Rather 
the toxin itself needs to be detected and identified. 
iii. The high toxicity of ricin demands for detection limits down to a few pg/ ml, 
especially when clinical samples are analyzed ( e.g. in the course of attempted 
suicides88) challenging current det
title: Recommended Operating Procedures for Analysis in the Verification of Chemical Disarmament

text:
iii. The high toxicity of ricin demands for detection limits down to a few pg/ ml, 
especially when clinical samples are analyzed ( e.g. in the course of attempted 
suicides88) challenging current detection technologies.

iv. Ricin is produced in different variants ( e.g. ricin D, ricin E) that vary on the 
molecular level. Additionally, the plant produces the highly similar RCA120 which 
has to be discerned from ricin. 
Currently, expert laboratories use an ever -increasing number of different technical 
approaches for detection, i dentification and quantification of ricin. Valuable in -house 
validation studies have been performed and published, presenting results obtained using 
individual technical approaches. However, there are no universally agreed reference 
methods available, nor is there a certified reference material (CRM) available for ricin. The 
lack of CRM clearly hampers any efforts to develop a harmonized quality assurance system. 
Expert laboratories mostly use in-house purified ricin or commercial toxin preparations of 
varying quality as quality control samples or for calibration, which makes objective 
comparison of accuracy and sensitivity of different method
title: Recommended Operating Procedures for Analysis in the Verification of Chemical Disarmament

text:
use purified ricin or commercial toxin preparations of 
varying quality as quality control samples or for calibration, which makes objective 
comparison of accuracy and sensitivity of different methods questionable. 
 
In this situation the EU-funded project EQuATox (www.equatox.eu; 2012–2014) started to 
work on basic quality requirements for ricin detection. The focus was on the generation and 
characterization of reference materials (RMs) both for ricin and for RCA120. 38 The RMs 
were used to organize a large international proficiency tes t (PT), taking into account 
detection of different levels of toxin spiked into buffer and complex matrices.33 
By definition, PTs are performed to e valuate the participants ’ performance against pre -
established criteria by comparing their measurement results with assigned values and with 
results obtained in other laboratories. In this type of interlaboratory study, the participants 
are generally free in the choice of the analytical method that should be consistent with their 
normal routine practice. 97 , 98 This approac h is usually performed prior to m ethod 
performance studies assessing the characteristics and performance of individu
title: Recommended Operating Procedures for Analysis in the Verification of Chemical Disarmament

text:
at should be consistent with their 
normal routine practice. 97 , 98 This approac h is usually performed prior to m ethod 
performance studies assessing the characteristics and performance of individual methods. 
 
Within the EQuATox PT on ricin detection and identification from aqueous solutions, nine 
samples were distributed containing ricin or RCA120 spiked into buffer, milk, and meat 
extract at concentrations ranging from 500 µg/ml to 500 pg/ ml. Additionally, a solid 
material, an organic fertilizer containing R. communis shred, was distributed. 17 expert 
laboratories from 12 countries participated in the exercise and applied a range of different 
immunological, spectrometric and functional approaches.37 
 
The PT confirmed that ELISAs are the most sensitive methods of all analytical approaches 
applied and identified four different ELISAs base d on monoclonal antibodies (mAb) 
delivering correct and equivalent results on the materials tested .33 Furthermore, the PT 
proved that several MS-based approaches had excellent selectivity between the two related 
lectins ricin and RCA120, allowing for unambiguous identification of both analytes. Among 
the methods applied were pro
title: Recommended Operating Procedures for Analysis in the Verification of Chemical Disarmament

text:
t several MS-based approaches had excellent selectivity between the two related 
lectins ricin and RCA120, allowing for unambiguous identification of both analytes. Among 
the methods applied were protocols applying LC-ESI MS/MS and MALDI-TOF MS. With 
respect to functional assays, two different approaches were successfully used on the samples 
provided: an MS-based method detecting the adenine release from an artificial substrate and 
an in vitro cytotoxicity assay based on impedance measurement. 
In order to identify good analytical practices, the different technical approaches applied were 
grouped according to their detection principle and statistically analy sed to obtain success 
rates. The success rates on all samples ranged from 71.5–77.7% when all nine samples were 
considered corresponding to similar overall success rates for the different methods. However, 
a closer look on the individual samples revealed differences for the different technical 
approaches and helped to visualize advantages and limitations of different techn ical 
approaches: Comparing samples containing high concentrations of either ricin or RCA120,

A Biotoxin Confidence building exercise on ricin was organized by OPCW in January 2017

9. Summary and future developments 
As described in this chapter there are different methods available for the detection and 
identification of ricin based on immunological, spectrometric and functional approaches or 
combinations thereof. Currently only a limited number of approaches has been evaluate

identification of ricin based on immunological, spectrometric and functional approaches or 
combinations thereof. Currently only a limited number of approaches has been evaluated in 
PTs or method performance studies.33 Considering the two PTs performed in the framework 
of EQuATox and OPCW, immunoassays generally exhibited better sensitivity and needed 
only minimal sample preparation – usually simple dilution of complex matrices in order to 
reduce interference by potential inhibitors or cross reactive analytes – compared to MS -
based methods. This indicates the need to develop simple but more effective sample 
preparation procedures for MS-based methods with a high confirmative power to eliminate 
as many interfering substances as possible before the detection step. In addition and in 
parallel to the important issue of sample preparation, the evaluation of stand -alone or 
hyphenated mass spectrometry methods, which offer more reliable toxin identification and, 
in the medium term, accurate quantification of biological toxins, will gain in creased

1. Scope 
This chapter describes the identification of ricin by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay 
(ELISA). There are various formats of ELISA for the detection of specific soluble antigens, 
antibody-sandwich ELISA may be the most useful immunoassay for antigen detection due 
to its sensitivity and specificity. The sandw
title: Recommended Operating Procedures for Analysis in the Verification of Chemical Disarmament

text:
us formats of ELISA for the detection of specific soluble antigens, 
antibody-sandwich ELISA may be the most useful immunoassay for antigen detection due 
to its sensitivity and specificity. The sandwich ELISA is based on the interactions of 
capturing antibody (Ab I) immobilized on solid material and its antigen (ricin). This complex 
is then detected by a specific detection antibody (Ab II) labelled with an enzyme for 
visualization. 
2. Summary of the method 
 A protocol using detection antibody conjugated to horseradish peroxidase (HRP) in a direct 
sandwich ELISA is provided. However, other approaches such as the use of unconjugated 
detection antibody followed by a secondary antibody-HRP, or biotinylated detection 
antibody followed by streptavidin-HRP, are also appropriate. After unbound conjugates are 
removed, a chromogenic or chemiluminescent substrate is added and a coloured or 
chemiluminescent product is generated , respectively . Finally, the product is detected 
visually or with a microtiter plate reader. The conventional colorimetric method will provide 
an end-point reading, while the chemiluminescent method detects light in a transient reaction 
that will only app
title: Recommended Operating Procedures for Analysis in the Verification of Chemical Disarmament

text:
or with a microtiter plate reader. The conventional colorimetric method will provide 
an end-point reading, while the chemiluminescent method detects light in a transient reaction 
that will only appear while the enzyme -substrate reaction is occurring. The 
chemiluminescence ELISA has a superior sensitivity compared to the conventional ELISA 
for the same pair of sandwiching antibodies.

The antibodies for ricin-specific sandwich ELISA should ideally be chosen to detect two 
ricin epitopes. A good strategy will be to choose an antibody to Ricin A -chain, another 
antibody to Ricin B-chain. 
All laboratories are encouraged to modify and optimize their ELISA based on the supporting 
protocol provided in this chapter. 
3. Safety aspects 
Since ricin is a type II ribosome-inactiving protein with high toxicity, all experiments should 
be performed in accordance to biosafety guidelines. All contacts with the active toxin should 
be avoided, by protective gloves and goggles. 
After analysis, samples containing ricin should be decontaminated by approved methods1, 2. 
A recommended procedure is to heat all ricin-distributed solutions for an hour at 100 °C and 
then treat them with, e.g. alkali for the total denaturation and detoxication of the ricin. 
4. Handling and storing of samples 
All ricin -containing samples should be handled with care to avoid contamination w
title: Recommended Operating Procedures for Analysis in the Verification of Chemical Disarmament

text:
them with, e.g. alkali for the total denaturation and detoxication of the ricin. 
4. Handling and storing of samples 
All ricin -containing samples should be handled with care to avoid contamination with 
foreign materials which could give false -positive reactions and to prevent cross -
contamination between positive and negative samples. Ricin samples should be kept cold 
during handling and stored in a freezer as soon as possible. Avoid freeze/thaw cycles in all 
samples containing protein. 
5. Methods and Materials 
5.1 ELISA instrument 
Microplate reader with absorbance or chemiluminescence mode.

are given in Table 1.

6. Recommended ELISA conditions 
Recommended absorbance or chemiluminescence ELISA conditions are given in Table 2. 
Primary antibody I, the “capture antibody”, is passively adsorbed onto the solid phase of the 
plate to capture ricin. Primary antibody II, the “detection antibody”, is an HRP -labelled 
conjugate used to bind ricin to complete the sandwich format. Either mono clonal or 
polyclonal antibodies can be used as the capture and detection antibodies. It is recommended 
that at least one of the antibodies to be a monoclonal antibody, as the inherent 
monospecificity toward a single epitope in a m
title: Recommended Operating Procedures for Analysis in the Verification of Chemical Disarmament

text:
can be used as the capture and detection antibodies. It is recommended 
that at least one of the antibodies to be a monoclonal antibody, as the inherent 
monospecificity toward a single epitope in a monoclonal antibody improves specificity of 
the assay. A polyclonal antibody is often selected to improve the sensitivity of the assay. A 
binding optimization should be carried out, and the antibody with the better binding affinity 
should be used as the capture antibody. 
The experimental conditions in absorbance or chemiluminescence ELISA may be modified 
according to the type of sample. The typical volumes used for general reagents and samples 
are 50– 300 µl per well. In direct sandwich ELISA, the samples do not have to be purified 
before analysis is performed. 
Note! The quality (including the binding affinity, specificity and purity) of the antibodies are 
the key factor in developing a sensitive and robust ELISA. In the case of ricin ELISA, the 
cross-reactivity of anti-ricin antibodies to RCA120 has to be investigated as well.

7. Quality control 
Before developing a new ELISA, a selection process should be included to choose microtiter 
plates with the most desired binding properties. The plate should produce hi gh signal for 
positive control samples, yet maintaining very low background noise. To avoid batch to 
batch differences, more than one batch (typically 3) of the chosen microtiter plates should 
be tested and qualified.

be tested and qualified. 
After ELISA method has been developed, ELISA plates can be produced , stabilized with 
commercial stabilizer and vacuum-sealed for long term stockpile. 
The performance of the ELISA can be monitored by a series of quality control samples. The 
quality control (QC) should include a positive control (ricin in a defined concentration spiked 
in a certain matrix), a negative control (a matrix without ricin), a blank control (wells 
containing PBST diluents only), a detection conjugate control (a non -capture antibody,

substrate control (a well without HRP-Ab, which represents non-enzymatic production). All 
controls are advised to assay in triplicates in a “QC plate” after every 5 sample plates. During

Control and standard measurements have to meet the acceptance criteria (determined during

8. Analysis of samples 
8.1 Preparation of sample for analysis 
The passive binding of antibodies and proteins to the antibodies immobilized on microplate 
surface make it easy to sep arate bound and unbound material during the assay. The ability 
to wash away non-specific materials makes ELISA a powerful tool for detecting the specific 
analytes. A numbe

text:

to wash away non-specific materials makes ELISA a powerful tool for detecting the specific 
analytes. A number of modifications toward the basic procedure of ELISA can be performed. 
A highly specific interaction between antigen and antibodies is the most crucial point in the 
detection strategy of ELISA. In the direct sandwich ELISA, antibody reagents are 
standardized, i.e. the optimal dilutions of the capture antibody and the HRP labelled antibody 
(i.e. the detection conjugate) are determined by checkerboard titration. Once optimum 
working dilutions are established, they are used for sequential assays of all quality control 
and sample analyses. 
The samples homogenised in buffer are added into respective wells (duplicates or triplicates). 
Two-fold serial dilution range of each sample is recommended. For quantitative analys is, 
reference standards (duplicates or triplicates) as well as blank samples (duplicates or 
triplicates) are run in each plat e to ensure accuracy. The concentrations of the reference 
standards should cover the dynamic range.

8.2 Identification 
Identification is established by comparing the signal intensity of the samples against the 
positive threshold. Generally, three standard deviations above the mean value of the negative 
control can be used to establish the positive threshold. The mean value of the 
duplicates/triplicates sample wells is compared to the threshold value to determine the 
positive or negative status of test samples. 
To include quantification in this assay , a standard curve can be prepared from the data 
generated by the serially diluted reference standards, with reference standard’s concentration 
on the x-axis (log. scale) and signal intensity on the y-axis (log. scale). The concentration of 
ricin in the sample can be interpolated from this standard curve.

The analytical and systematic characteristics of sandwich ELISA makes it suitable as a 
screening test to analyse large number of samples . The samples suspected to contain ricin

9.2 Advantages/Disadvantages 
Sandwich ELISAs are some of the most sensitive detection technologies routinely used in 
the laboratories. Their limit of detection can range from pf/ml to ng/ml, depending on the 
properties of the chosen antibodies, and the signal development method. 
Compared to conventional colorimetric method, chemiluminescence ELISA has a superior 
sensitivity due to the enhanced signal development provided by the continuous enzymatic 
conversion of substrate to chemiluminescent signal. It can potentially lower the limit o f 
detection to the pg/ml level. ELISA is also a high throughput and cost-effective method that 
compliment mass-spectrometric based ricin detection method. 
The limitation of direct sandwich ELISA is the need for a labelled primary Ab II. Another 
limitation is that the analyte (ricin) must have at least two epitopes: one for capture a
title: Recommended Operating Procedures for Analysis in the Verification of Chemical Disarmament

text:
detection method. 
The limitation of direct sandwich ELISA is the need for a labelled primary Ab II. Another 
limitation is that the analyte (ricin) must have at least two epitopes: one for capture antibody 
and one for detection antibody. ELISA techniques are also not able to distinguish between 
biologically active and inactive forms of ricin. The latter can be overcome by p airing an 
antibody recognizing ricin A chain with another antibody recognizing ricin B chain, 
especially one that recognise the conformational epitope. The inactive ricin may not be 
detected, as shown by the matched antibodies pair of 3D74 and 4C133. 
Currently, the ELISA is not able to reliably distinguish ricin from the highly homologous 
RCA120 in a mixture assuming that both proteins are present in significant amounts, a task 
that might be relevant in the course of a forensic investigation.

1. Scope 
This chapter describes the enrichment of ricin through the use of immunocapture. Magnetic 
beads (MB)-based immunocapture of ricin presented here is based on the efficiency of the 
monoclonal antibody (mAb) directed against ricin to interact specifical ly with its epi
title: Recommended Operating Procedures for Analysis in the Verification of Chemical Disarmament

text:
munocapture. Magnetic 
beads (MB)-based immunocapture of ricin presented here is based on the efficiency of the 
monoclonal antibody (mAb) directed against ricin to interact specifical ly with its epitope. 
Streptavidin-coated magnetic beads can specifically capture the ricin complex and its 
biotinylated anti-ricin mAb. Enriched ricin can be detected with different detection methods. 
2. Summary of the method 
Here a MB-based technique is recommended to immunocapture ricin using a mAb directed 
against the B -chain of ricin via streptavidin -biotin interaction. This preconcentration and 
clean-up technique is a good fit to enrich the target protein and remove the unrelated but 
highly abundant proteins in the matrix. 
Generally, in immuno -purification, a specific antibody is conjugated to an insoluble 
substrate (e.g. agarose beads or magnetic beads). This is achieved through interaction with 
either protein A or G or through covalent linkage with t he substrate surface. Once the 
antibody is bound, the beads are exposed to a complex mixture of proteins containing the 
target protein (the antigen). Through the specific antibody, the target protein will be bound 
to the immunocapt
title: Recommended Operating Procedures for Analysis in the Verification of Chemical Disarmament

text:
tibody is bound, the beads are exposed to a complex mixture of proteins containing the 
target protein (the antigen). Through the specific antibody, the target protein will be bound 
to the immunocapture bait. Following this binding, the antigen -coupled surface may be 
washed and after that, the target protein can be eluted from the beads. This basic principle 
of immuno-purification may be varied according to the surface type as well as the antibody 
coupling method.

3. Safety aspects 
Since ricin is a ribosome-inactiving protein type II with high toxicity, all related experiments 
should be performed according to the operating biosafety guidelines. All contact with the 
active toxins should be avoided and protectiv e gloves and goggles should be worn during 
sample treatment and analysis. 
After analysis, samples containing ricin should be totally decontaminated. A recommended 
procedure is to heat all ricin-distributed solutions for an hour at 100 °C and then treat them 
with, e.g. alkali lye to make sure all ricin is fully denatured and detoxicated. 
4. Handling and storing of samples 
All ricin samples should be handled with care to avoid contamination with foreign materials 
which could give false -positive reactions and to prevent cross -contamination between 
positive and negative samples. Ricin samples should be kept cold during handling and stored 
in the freezer as soon as possible. Avoid freeze/thaw cycles in all samples

positive and negative samples. Ricin samples should be kept cold during handling and stored 
in the freezer as soon as possible. Avoid freeze/thaw cycles in all samples containing protein.

7. Quality control 
In the quality control (QC) test for such an immunocapture technique, pure ricin with known 
concentration in PBS can be used as a positive control. 
Since BSA-containing PBS solution (PBS/BSA) has been recommended to maintain the 
bioactivity of streptavidin and anti-ricin antibodies, and to reduce nonspecific bindings, the 
enrichment efficiency depends mainly upon the specificity and binding capacity of the 
antibody, while the potential interference of unrelated proteins that occurred in matrix is 
avoided. 
The enrichment efficiency is heavily dependent on the per formance of the biotinylation of 
antibodies and the binding capacity of streptavidin with biotinylated antibodies. 
Initially, the optimi zation of the biotinylation of the antibodies should be performed. The 
titration experiment to determine the required a mount of biotinylated antibodies versus the 
required amount of streptavidin -MBs should also be performed before the immunocapt
title: Recommended Operating Procedures for Analysis in the Verification of Chemical Disarmament

text:
uld be performed. The 
titration experiment to determine the required a mount of biotinylated antibodies versus the 
required amount of streptavidin -MBs should also be performed before the immunocapture 
of ricin from samples. The preparation of parallel samples is recommended. Disposable 
plastic tubes should be used to avoid cross-contamination. 
8. Evaluation of method 
8.1 Area of applicability 
This immunocapture technique can be applied to any kind of complicated samples, such as 
food, drinks, soil, water, plasma, serum, and tissues. Depending on the different binding 
capacities of streptavidin -coated MB towards biotinylated antibodies, and the different 
binding affinity and specificity of the anti -ricin antibody and ricin, the largest enrichment 
ratio is varied but is usually higher than tenfold. As well as providing an effective enrichment 
of the target, the technique can also be used to remove the background which may cause 
potential interference. 
8.2 Advantages/Disadvantages 
The advantages of this immunocapture technique are its specificity, reliability and simplicity. 
The t echnique is quite suitable to be employed before mass spectrometr ic identification 
m

text:
dvantages 
The advantages of this immunocapture technique are its specificity, reliability and simplicity. 
The t echnique is quite suitable to be employed before mass spectrometr ic identification 
methods, especially for the effective extraction of ricin from complicated samples. 
The main disadvantage of this immunocapture technique is that the optimization of several 
involved procedures are still needed to ensure the highest level of efficiency. At the moment, 
only common recommendations can be followed. Another disadvantage of the method is 
that it may also pull down the related RCA120 from a ricin/RCA120 mixture due to the little 
cross-reactivity of the antibody. 
Note! Here the described immunocapture method is only focused on the antigen capture via 
streptavidin coated magnetic bead -biotinylated mAb bait. Other appropriate sample 
preparation procedures are also suitable, such as immunoprecipitation using commercial 
Protein A/G Magnetic Beads. In addition to immunocapture, other affinity capture method 
can be also considered. For example, ricin consists of a galactose residue-binding B chain, 
the samples can be first ly captured by p-aminobenzyl 1 -thio-β-D-galacto

1. Scope 
This chapter describes the detection, identification and activity determination of ricin using 
matrix-assisted laser desorption/ioni

1. Scope 
This chapter describes the detection, identification and activity determination of ricin using 
matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization mass spectrometry ( MALDI-MS) and tandem 
mass spectrometry (MS/MS). Ricin is a highly toxic plant protein found in the seeds of 
Ricinus communis, a perennial shrub of the spurge family Euphorbiaceae, and belongs to 
the family of type II ribosome -inactivating (RIP-II) proteins. The holotoxin (~64 kDa) 
consists of a carbohydrate-binding B chain (~34 kDa) , linked via a disulphide bond to the 
catalytically active A chain (~32 kDa). The RNA N-glycosidase activity of the A chain leads 
to depurination of a single adenine from a position known as the sarcin/ricin tetraloop in the 
28S rRNA contained in the 60S subunit of the ribosome. During translation, this 
depurination event prevents binding of elongation factor 2, ultimately resulting in cell death. 
Ricin has a high sequence homology (> 93% between A-chains and 84% between B-chains) 
to the much less toxic protein R. communis agglutinin (RCA120) also present in the seeds. 
Ricin is listed as a Schedule 1 compound of the Ch
title: Recommended Operating Procedures for Analysis in the Verification of Chemical Disarmament

text:
omology (> 93% between A-chains and 84% between B-chains) 
to the much less toxic protein R. communis agglutinin (RCA120) also present in the seeds. 
Ricin is listed as a Schedule 1 compound of the Chemical Weapons Convention (CWC) and 
the Biological Weapons Convention (BWC). 
MALDI-MS as a soft ionisation technique allows for the rapid and easy analysis of large 
non-volatile labile biomolecules like ricin or ricin-derived peptides, with minim al sample 
preparation. Under standard conditions, MALDI-MS generates mostly singl y charged 
protonated molecules that produce spectra that are straightforward to interpret. This coupled 
with the theoretically unlimited mass range obtainable using a time-of-flight (TOF) analyser 
and the possibility for high-throughput analysis makes MALDI-MS one of the spectrometric
title: Recommended Operating Procedures for Analysis in the Verification of Chemical Disarmament

text:
RECOMMENDED OPERATION PROCEDURES FOR CWC-RELATED ANALYSIS 
Section 3. Analytical methods

Date 11 December 2017 Page 596 
methods of choice for the detection, identification and activity determination of ricin. In the 
course of an investigation, MALDI -MS is typically used to confirm results obtained by 
screening approaches, such as lateral flow assays, biosensor or ELISA techniques. 
2. Summary of the method 
MALDI-MS is suitable for the following: a) rapid ricin detection as the intact protein by 
highly accurate molecular weight determination in sample matrices of low complexity; b) 
ricin detection based upon enzymatically digested peptides by peptide mass fingerprinting 
(PMF) or unambiguous identification by MS/MS amino acid sequencing; and c) activity 
determination using the adenine release assay (Table 1). The lack of a suitable separation 
technique coupled online to the MALDI ion source like liquid or gas chromatography 
systems in front of an electrospray ionisation (ESI) source means that either analyte 
enrichment and/or prefractionation techniques are essential for complex sa
title: Recommended Operating Procedures for Analysis in the Verification of Chemical Disarmament

text:
rce like liquid or gas chromatography 
systems in front of an electrospray ionisation (ESI) source means that either analyte 
enrichment and/or prefractionation techniques are essential for complex sample matrixes or 
highly diluted samples to reduce background interferences and/or to increase the analyte’s 
concentration prior to MS analysis . This is especially important for activity measurement . 
To this end, affinity enrichment using anti-ricin antibodies (preferably monoclonal) or 
carbohydrates coupled to magnetic beads is frequently used. Alte rnatively, analyte 
separation by SDS-PAGE followed by enzymatic in-gel digestion is also used for sample 
preparation. 
As stated previously, MALDI ion sources do not have the capability for online introduction 
of the analytes from a separation technique such as liquid or gas chromatography. However 
spotting robots are commercially available that enable online deposition of matrix and the 
flow through from a separation of the enzymatically digested peptides using liquid 
chromatography onto a number of spots on a MALDI target. The distribution of the peptide 
mixture on to multiple spots means that both highly complex and dilute s
title: Recommended Operating Procedures for Analysis in the Verification of Chemical Disarmament

text:
cally digested peptides using liquid 
chromatography onto a number of spots on a MALDI target. The distribution of the peptide 
mixture on to multiple spots means that both highly complex and dilute samples can be 
analysed using unambiguous identification by MS/MS amino acid sequencing. 
Quality control tests must be conducted prior to ricin measurements. A positive control using 
a highly purified ricin standard verifies the correct performance of the instrument and a blank 
test verifies the absence of any traces of ricin. Screening for ricin is performed by peptide 
mass fingerprinting using a minimum of two proteotypic peptides from both the A-chain and 
the B-chain (see Appendix). Unambiguous identification of ricin is made by comparison of 
the measured MS/MS spectrum to that of a known ricin reference standard or by a database 
search for proteotypic peptides (see Appendix). In the case of activity determination, the 
enrichment step using ricin-specific antibodies confers specificity to the method since other 
bacterial and plant toxins also induce adenine release from the same sarcin/ricin tetraloop. 
The functional test is based upon monitoring the adenine release from a
title: Recommended Operating Procedures for Analysis in the Verification of Chemical Disarmament

text:
ificity to the method since other 
bacterial and plant toxins also induce adenine release from the same sarcin/ricin tetraloop. 
The functional test is based upon monitoring the adenine release from an artificial DNA or 
RNA substrate which mimics the toxin’s natural RNA target.

3. Safety aspects 
Ricin is a highly toxic protein that requires appropriate safety measures. It is recommended 
to handle the toxin using a class II vertical laminar flow cabinet in a dedicated toxin 
laboratory. Individual protective equipment such as a laboratory coat, gloves, and safety 
glasses are essential. Toxin-containing solutions are inactivated by dilution in alkaline 
solutions e.g. 5% sodium hydroxide (equivalent to approx. 1.3 M NaOH) overnight while 
solid waste materials are inactivated by autoclaving ( e.g. 134°C, 1 h , 30 psi ). In general, 
MALDI–MS analysis of enzymatically digested ricin ( and thus functionally inactivated 
toxin) co-crystallized in MALDI–MS matrix does not require specific safety precautions. 
4. Instrumentation 
4.1 MALDI-MS instrument 
Any modern MALDI–MS instrument that covers a mass range of m/z 600–4500 can be used 
for peptide mass fingerprinting or adenine release activity determination of ricin. If a time-
of-flight (TOF) mas
title: Recommended Operating Procedures for Analysis in the Verification of Chemical Disarmament

text:
Any modern MALDI–MS instrument that covers a mass range of m/z 600–4500 can be used 
for peptide mass fingerprinting or adenine release activity determination of ricin. If a time-
of-flight (TOF) mass analyser is used a reflector mode is essential. For molecular weight 
determination of intact ricin (~64 kDa) a TOF analyser operated in linear mode with a mass 
range of at least 130 kDa is desirable. The increased mass range will also allow for the 
molecular weight determination of intact RCA120 (~120 kDa). For unambiguous 
identification of tryptic digested ricin by MS/MS amino acid sequencing, the MALDI ion 
source has to be coupled to a tandem mass spectrometer like a TOF/TOF analyser. It is 
feasible to use o ther high resolution mass spectrometry analysers like FT–ICR (Fourier 
transform ion cyclotron resonance) or Orbitrap coupled with a MALDI ion source. These, 
however, are not routinely used and will not be explained in this chapter. 
4.2 MALDI matrix 
Several different MALDI matrices are available for intact protein and peptide mass 
spectrometry analysis, each with its own advantages and disadvantages. Suitable matrices, 
matrix buffers as well as different matrix cryst
title: Recommended Operating Procedures for Analysis in the Verification of Chemical Disarmament

text:
matrices are available for intact protein and peptide mass 
spectrometry analysis, each with its own advantages and disadvantages. Suitable matrices, 
matrix buffers as well as different matrix crystal layer techniques should be tested for every 
unknown sample composition. Recommended matrices (ɑ-cyano-4-hydroxycinnamic acid, 
sinapinic acid) and procedures for ricin analysis by MALDI–TOF MS are described in the 
experimental section. 
4.3 Reagents and chemicals 
To date, r icin and RCA120 reference material s are not commercially available. In this 
situation, most laboratories use in-house materials of different purity and activity as quality 
control samples. For information, t horoughly characterized ricin and RCA120 materials 
have been prepared as part of the European Union-funded project EQuATox and a consensus 
concentration has been determined for the ricin material in an international proficiency 
test.1,2 This work sets the basis for further quality assurance measures and the future 
development of certified calibrants and reference materials. 
Additional chemicals for the different MALDI-MS detection and identification techniques 
are given in Tables 2 to 4.

5. Experimental 
5.1 Molecular weight determination of the intact ricin protein 
When searching for an indication of ricin in a given sample, the detection of the intact ricin 
protein by MALDI-MS is an easy and rapid approach. However, the method is restricted to 
samples of low complexity and has a limit of detection of above 1 µg/ml.3 With an intact 
molecular weight of approximately 64 kDa, ricin can be distinguished from the highly 
homologous RCA120 protein (~120 kDa) with any MALDI–TOF instrument in positive ion 
linear acquisition mode.4 It is worth noting that many other proteins have the same 
approximate molecular weight as ricin , so this method do es not allow for unambiguous 
identification of the toxin. For quality control, a sample of a ricin reference material should 
be measured in parallel. Additionally, further methods delivering sequence information are 
highly recommended (C hapter part 5.2). A recommended procedure for molecular weight 
determination
title: Recommended Operating Procedures for Analysis in the Verification of Chemical Disarmament

text:
should 
be measured in parallel. Additionally, further methods delivering sequence information are 
highly recommended (C hapter part 5.2). A recommended procedure for molecular weight 
determination by MALDI–TOF MS is given below and r eagents and chemicals are 
summarized in Table 2. 
For molecular weight determination, the sample suspected of containing ricin is mixed with 
an equal amount of a BSA standard solution and the mixture diluted in a 1:1 ratio with 
MALDI matrix (saturated sinapinic acid solution in 70% ACN and 30% water with 0.01% 
TFA). MALDI matrix is diluted 1:1 with water and one µl of this solution is deposited on a 
steel target and dried at room temperature . One µl of the sample/BSA/MALDI matrix 
mixture is then spotted onto the dried droplet layer and also dried at room temperature. Once 
dried, e ach prepared spot is washed by layering 2.5 µl of 0.1% TFA over the spot for 
10 seconds after which the remaining liquid is removed using a pipette. External calibration 
of the instrument is performed for a suitable mass range according to the manufacturer’s 
instructions. Internal calibration is done using the detected charged variants (M+1) 1+ and 
(M+2)2+ of
title: Recommended Operating Procedures for Analysis in the Verification of Chemical Disarmament

text:
tion 
of the instrument is performed for a suitable mass range according to the manufacturer’s 
instructions. Internal calibration is done using the detected charged variants (M+1) 1+ and 
(M+2)2+ of the spiked BSA standard. It is recommended to use the d efault settings of the 
mass spectrometer for positive ion linear acquisition mode with a minimum mass range of 
m/z 10000 to 130000 as summarized in Table 5. Representative results are shown in Figure 1.

5.2 Peptide mass fingerprinting and MS/MS of enzymatically digested ricin protein 
Peptide mass fingerprinting (PMF) is a widely accepted mass spectrometry based proteomic 
approach to detect high molecular weight proteins such as ricin. Prior to analysis, ricin is 
digested by an endo peptidase (e.g. trypsin, chymotrypsin) into peptides and the resulting 
peptide mixture is analysed by MALDI–TOF MS. Acquired peptide mass lists are compared 
to theoretically in-silico digested proteins via a database search. Using this basic approach, 
ricin can be differentiated from RCA120 and other proteins. 
In order to obtain unambiguous
title: Recommended Operating Procedures for Analysis in the Verification of Chemical Disarmament

text:
e compared 
to theoretically in-silico digested proteins via a database search. Using this basic approach, 
ricin can be differentiated from RCA120 and other proteins. 
In order to obtain unambiguous information, this approach is extended by using tandem mass 
spectrometry (MALDI–TOF/TOF MS ) to generate fragmentation of the ricin specific 
peptides that delivers protein sequence information which unambiguously confirm s the 
identity of the analyte. 
For complex environmental, biological or food samples both approaches require 
prefractionation to obtain reasonable sensitivity . This is frequently achieved using affinity 
enrichment by anti -ricin antibodies coupled to magnetic beads. 4,5 In this approach, either 
monoclonal or polyclonal antibodies can be used. However, each should be tested for their 
specific read-out (i.e. PMF or MS/MS versus activity measurement [Chapter part 5.3]) as 
not all available antibodies perform equally well for each read-out5 and the specific epitope 
recognised by different antibodies can enhance the enrichment of the analyte. If antibodies 
of sufficient quality are not available, enrichment by carbohydrates coupled to microbeads 
is an alternati
title: Recommended Operating Procedures for Analysis in the Verification of Chemical Disarmament

text:
recognised by different antibodies can enhance the enrichment of the analyte. If antibodies 
of sufficient quality are not available, enrichment by carbohydrates coupled to microbeads 
is an alternative.6 Carbohydrate-based affinity purification has the advantage of extracting 
all potential RIP-II proteins from a given sample thus making them accessible to MS-based 
differentiation, but the strategy is hampered or even fails with sample matrices such as milk 
that contain an abundance of certain carbohydrates due to the ir competition with lectin 
binding.4 Finally, in the absence of any affinity enrichment, the separation of sample

used for sample preparation. 
Alternatively, complex sample s can be enzymatically digested and the resultant peptide 
mixture separated using liquid chromatography and online deposition onto numerous spots 
on a MALDI target prior to MS measurement (LC MALDI). Using this technique, the tryptic 
peptides from a digestion can be distributed on numerous spots (usually ~ 96 but up to 384) 
rather than only one. Following deposition, the target is analysed using a da ta dependent 
MS/MS method. B enefits of this type of analysis are that the pe ptides are 'stored' on the 
respective spots which enables even less abundant peptides to be both identified in MS mode 
and their MS/MS mass spectrum acquired; and it simplifies the mass spectrum obtained from 
each individual spot thus increasing the total number of tryptic peptides that can be observed.

each individual spot thus increasing the total number of tryptic peptides that can be observed. 
The distribution of the peptide mixture on multiple spots and the fact that the MS/MS mass 
spectra are acquired off -line means that both complex and dilute samples can be analysed 
with this method. This analysis can also be done following affinity enrichment of the sample. 
Information on i mmunoaffinity procedures are described in Section 3, Part F, Chapter V: 
Analysis of ricin: immunocapture. Reagents and chemicals for PMF and MS/MS of t ryptic 
ricin peptides are given in Table 3. 
For affinity enrichment, 500 µl of the sample suspected of containing ricin is mixed for 1 h 
under constant agitation with 20 µl of tosyl-activated paramagnetic Dynabeads coated with 
an antibody directed against ricin. After washing the beads twice with PBS/Tween and water, 
bound toxin is eluted from the beads with 25 µl of 0.1% TFA. Beads are removed from the 
solution and the toxin solution neutralized by the addition of 7 µl of 400 mM ammonium 
bicarbonate buffer. Disulphide bonds are reduced by adding 1.5 µl of 400 mM dithiothreitol 
in w
title: Recommended Operating Procedures for Analysis in the Verification of Chemical Disarmament

text:
moved from the 
solution and the toxin solution neutralized by the addition of 7 µl of 400 mM ammonium 
bicarbonate buffer. Disulphide bonds are reduced by adding 1.5 µl of 400 mM dithiothreitol 
in water and heating the sample at 95°C for 10 min. The sample is cooled to RT and alkylated 
by adding 3 µl of 500 mM iodoacetamide in water and incubating at RT for 30 min in the 
dark. Toxin digestion is achieved by adding 5 µl of trypsin solution (20 ng/µl) and heating 
at 37°C for 17 hours. If time is a consideration, it is advis ed to shorten the incubation time 
by using a rapid solvent-assisted trypsin digestion for one hour as described in Östin et al., 
2007.7 The peptide solution is cleaned and enriched by a C18 ZipTip procedure according 
to the manufacturer’s recommendations. One µl of the purified peptide solution is mixed 
with 1 µl of MALDI matrix (12 mg /ml HCCA in 0.1% TFA and ACN 1: 2) and 1 µl is 
deposited on a steel target and dried at room temperature. Samples, QC standards, and blank 
samples should be spotted in replicates. 
For LC MALDI, the sample can be analysed neat (25 µl); concentrated via protein 
precipitation using a tenfold dilution into acetone and resus
title: Recommended Operating Procedures for Analysis in the Verification of Chemical Disarmament

text:
rds, and blank 
samples should be spotted in replicates. 
For LC MALDI, the sample can be analysed neat (25 µl); concentrated via protein 
precipitation using a tenfold dilution into acetone and resuspen ded in 25 µl of 50 mM 
ammonium bicarbonate; or by affinity enrichment as described above. Tryptic digestion with 
reduction/alkylation can be undertaken as described above or the reduction/alkylation s teps 
can be omitted if the tryptic peptide representing the inter-disulphide bond between the two 
chains is desired. The observation of this peptide indicates that the protein is still intact – 
a requirement for bioactivity. Following digestion, the reaction is stopped with the addition 
of 2 µl of 10% TFA and pH confirmed to be >3. The peptide mixture is separated and spotted 
onto a MALDI target using a nano UPLC operated in preconcentration mode and a spotting 
robot as summarised in Table 7. A blank demons trating no carryover from the LC column 
and a ricin reference standard enzymatically digested under the same conditions should also 
be spotted. 
The MALDI-MS instrument is operated in positive ion reflector mode, with a mass range of 
600 to 4500 m/z (Table 5) . Deflect i

text:

be spotted. 
The MALDI-MS instrument is operated in positive ion reflector mode, with a mass range of 
600 to 4500 m/z (Table 5) . Deflect ion for matrix suppression is set to 600. External

5.3 Depurination activity assay 
In the course of a forensic investigation, it is important to determine the functionality of any 
ricin detected in order to assess the potential health threat posed by the material found. To 
this end, different functional approaches including MS -based depurination activity assays 
have been established.2,4 For monitoring the activity of ricin by MALDI–TOF MS, 
immunoaffinity extraction using antibodies directed against the ricin B chain is 
recommended since i) anti-B chain antibodies do not interfere with the A chain’s activity 
and ii) the presence of the holo -toxin can be demonstrated ( i.e. enrichment by the B chain, 
activity measurement by the A chain). In general, immunoaffinity enrichment provides 
specificity to ricin, since other plant and bacterial toxins such as abrin or shiga toxins can 
also induce adenine release from the same sarcin/ricin tetraloop of the 28S rRNA and without 
immunoaffinity enrichment this activity coul
title: Recommended Operating Procedures for Analysis in the Verification of Chemical Disarmament

text:
plant and bacterial toxins such as abrin or shiga toxins can 
also induce adenine release from the same sarcin/ricin tetraloop of the 28S rRNA and without 
immunoaffinity enrichment this activity could not be ascribed to ricin. Since the method 
does not sup ply unambiguous sequence information, it is best supplemented with PMF 
and/or MS/MS-based methods described under chapter part 5.2. 
Reagents and chemicals needed for activity assay are given in Table 4. 
For the depurination assay, t he r icin containing sample (500 µl) is mixed for 1 h under 
constant agitation with 20 µl of tosyl-activated paramagnetic Dynabeads coated with 
antibodies directed against ricin. After washing the beads twice with PBS/Tween and water, 
the beads are transferred to 20 µl of activity buffer (10 mM ammonium citrate and 1 mM 
EDTA, pH 4.0) 8 containing 200 µM RNA or DNA o ligonucleotide 
(5’--GCGCGAGAGCGC-3’) substrate which mimics the natural ribosomal RNA target of 
the toxin. The reaction is incubated at 37°C for 4 h. After incubation, 2 µl of the reaction 
solution is mixed with 18 µl of MALDI matrix (50 0 mM 3-Hydroxypicolinic acid and 
10 mM ammonium tartrate in 50% ACN and 50% water). One µl
title: Recommended Operating Procedures for Analysis in the Verification of Chemical Disarmament

text:
ed at 37°C for 4 h. After incubation, 2 µl of the reaction 
solution is mixed with 18 µl of MALDI matrix (50 0 mM 3-Hydroxypicolinic acid and 
10 mM ammonium tartrate in 50% ACN and 50% water). One µl is spotted onto a MALDI 
steel target and dried at room temperature. MALDI–TOF MS is operated in positive ion 
reflector mode with a mass range of 3000 to 4500 m/z. External calibration for a suitable 
mass range is performed according to the manufacture r’s instructions. Detection of ricin’s 
N-glycosidase activity is based on MALDI–TOF MS analysis of the intact substrate 
(m/z 3696) versus the depurinated DNA substrate ( m/z 3579) with a limit of detection of 
approximately 40 ng/ml (Figure 3).

8. Conclusion 
MALDI–TOF MS is one of the most important mass spectrometric technique s for the 
detection and identif ication of high molecular weight biomolecules such as ricin. In low 
complex sample mat rices, r icin can be detected by highly accurate molecular weight 
determination if µg/ml concentrations are present. Using enzymatic digestion followed by 
peptide mass fingerprinting provides additional specific identification data at low detectio n 
limits (ng/ml-range). It is recommended that at least two proteotypic peptides from both the 
A- and B -chain be detected and subjected to MS/MS amino acid sequencing to obtain 
unambiguous identification.

1. Scope 
This chapter describes methods for the unambiguous identification of intact ricin by liquid 
chomatography-electrospray ionization tandem mass spectrometry (LC –ESI/MS/MS). The 
methods include the following sequence of events: affinity capture of ricin and its analogues 
from aqueous samples or aqueous extracts of solid samples , enzymatic digestion of the 
proteins to the corresponding enzymatic peptides, separation of these peptides by liquid 
chromatography (LC) and their detection by tandem mass spectrometry. The enzyme of 
choice in this chapter is trypsin due to its selectivity and robustness. The methods are able 
to differentiate ricin from Ricinus communis agglutinin (RCA120) that has a highly 
homologous amino acid sequence to ricin and coexists with ricin in castor beans. 
This chapter also describes an approach for the measurement o
title: Recommended Operating Procedures for Analysis in the Verification of Chemical Disarmament

text:
Ricinus communis agglutinin (RCA120) that has a highly 
homologous amino acid sequence to ricin and coexists with ricin in castor beans. 
This chapter also describes an approach for the measurement of the N-glycosidase activity 
of the ricin present in a sample with LC–ESI/MS/MS by monitoring adenine released by 
ricin from a synthetic DNA oligonucleotide substrate with the GAGA tetraloop structure. 
The method includes the following sequence of events: affinity capture of ricin, incubation 
with a DNA substrate, separation and detection of released adenine by LC–MS/MS (SRM).

2. Safety aspects 
Exposure to ricin is hazardous to human health due to its activity as a ribosome-inactiving 
type II protein with high toxicity. All experiments related to ricin should be performed in A 
BSL-2 or BSL -3 cabinet with i ndividual protective equipment such as laboratory coat, 
gloves and safety goggles. 
After use, all solutions and consumptive material s contaminated with ricin must be 
decontaminated. Ricin can be decontaminated by different methods: 
(1) heat decontamination e.g. autoclaving (at 121 °C for 1 h at 15 psi); 
(2) chemical decontamination e.g. using bleach (1 to 2.5 %) or 2M NaOH for at least four 
hours.

3. LC-MS/MS analysis of ricin following tryptic digestion 
LC–MS/MS techniques are the most effective at differentiating ricin from RCA120 and 
other homologous proteins. The unambiguous identification can be completed by both non-
targeted and targeted peptide MS/MS analysis following tryptic digestion of ricin. Targeted 
peptide analysis can be performed by MS/MS ( SRM and Q-TOF/MS) that allows for an 
unambiguous identification of ricin using peptides unique to ricin. This approach only 
analyses for peptides unique to both the A and B chains of ricin and generally achieves 
detection of both. As such, this method can detect these ricin specific peptides with a very 
low limit of detection and can differentiate ricin from other homologous proteins. 
Non-targeted peptide analysis is performed using Q-TOF/MS in data-dependent MS/MS 
acquisition mode. This method has the potential to identify multiple tryptic peptides from 
both the A and B chains to unambiguously verify
title: Recommended Operating Procedures for Analysis in the Verification of Chemical Disarmament

text:
nalysis is performed using Q-TOF/MS in data-dependent MS/MS 
acquisition mode. This method has the potential to identify multiple tryptic peptides from 
both the A and B chains to unambiguously verify the presence of ricin but such high 
sequence coverage is usually only obtained in samples containing high concentrations of 
ricin. 
However, the introduction of a purification/enrichment step prior to tryptic digestion and 
LC–MS/MS analysis will increase the total amount of ricin while decreasing background 
interferences; making it possible to use LC–MS/MS identification techniques to 
unambiguously confirm the presence of ricin even in extremely dilute or complex samples. 
The process of LC–MS/MS analysis of ricin following tryptic digestion can be summarized 
as follows: ricin and RCA120 in aqueous samples are enriched using either 
galactopyranoside-agarose gel affinity or immunocapture and then digested with trypsin into 
peptides. The resulting tryptic peptides are detected by LC–ESI/MS/MS SRM or LC–ESI/Q-
TOF/MS. The reagents and chemicals needed for LC–ESI/MS/MS identification of the 
digested ricin are listed in Table 1.

3.1 Recommended procedures for affinity capture of ricin 
3.1.1 Galactose-agarose gel affinity capture 
The aqueous sample or aqueous extract of solid samples is applied to commercially available 
p-Aminobenzyl 1 -thio-β-D-galactopyranoside-Agarose ( PAG-Agarose) for the affinity 
capture of ricin and RCA120 based upon their specific affinity for the galactose ligand. 
Following incubation of the aqueous ricin -containing samples with PAG-Agarose 
equilibrated with PBS, the reaction gel solution is washed with PBS and then eluted with 
galactose in PBS. As a result, both ricin and RCA120 will be separated from aqueous sample 
or aqueous extract. However the volume is significantly increased after the elution as a result 
the eluate needs to be concentrated prior to digestion. Following concentration, the residual 
solution is reconstituted in 50 mM ammonium bicarbonate for effective digestion. The 
recommended procedures for PAG-Agarose affinity capture as used by RICD a
title: Recommended Operating Procedures for Analysis in the Verification of Chemical Disarmament

text:
. Following concentration, the residual 
solution is reconstituted in 50 mM ammonium bicarbonate for effective digestion. The

Any modern LC–ESI/MS/MS instrument with SRM scan mode such as a QqQ or QTRAP 
with a scan speed of at least 1 scan/sec and mass range of m/z 50–1000 can be used to detect 
the enzymatically digested specific pe

text:
LC–ESI/MS/MS instrument with SRM scan mode such as a QqQ or QTRAP 
with a scan speed of at least 1 scan/sec and mass range of m/z 50–1000 can be used to detect 
the enzymatically digested specific peptides. 
LC–ESI/MS/MS combined with an enzymatic digestion approach can provide a highly 
selective determination for target proteins. This selectively is crucial for the selection of 
specific and unique peptides for ricin due to the high amino acid seque nce homology 
between ricin and RCA120 that could result in a false positive determination for ricin. The 
tryptic peptides used for the determination of ricin should be chosen based upon the 
following criteria: specific ity to ricin, high MS response and not containing amino acid 
residues susceptible to chemical modification such as methionine, etc.

The tryptic peptides TA7, TA10, TA11, T A12, and T A13 from the A -chain and TB3, T B5, 
TB14, TB19 and T B20 from the B chain generated by tryptic digestion with reduction and 
alkylation of ricin have been shown to be the most sensitive and specific for ricin and are 
suitable for LC–ESI/MS/MS (SRM)
